title: Infosys, TCS stocks jump 2-3%, Nifty IT up over 2% as easing US Fed rate-hike fears boost tech stocks- Moneycontrol.com
summary: IT stocks led gains as Infosys and TCS rose 2-3% and the Nifty IT index climbed over 2% after easing expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate hike. A drop in crude oil prices following a pause in US-Iran military action reduced inflation concerns, lifting global risk appetite and supporting technology shares across indices.
content:
IT stocks led market gains on Monday, with heavyweights Infosys and TCS jumping 2-3 percent each, and the Nifty IT index climbing more than 2 percent as easing expectations of a US Federal Reserve interest rate hike boosted the rate-sensitive sector.

At 10:05 am, the Nifty IT index was up 2.25 percent, making it the top-performing sectoral index on the NSE. The broader market also traded higher, with the Sensex rising 533 points, or 0.7 percent, to 76,593, and the Nifty advancing 152 points, or 0.6 percent, to 23,920. Market breadth remained positive, with 2,569 shares advancing against 868 declining, while the India VIX fell 5.63 percent.

Four of the country's five largest IT companies featured among the top gainers on the Nifty 50. Infosys rose 2.98 percent, Tech Mahindra gained 2.38 percent, TCS advanced 2.11 percent and HCL Technologies added 2.10 percent. LTIMindtree was up 1.96 percent, while Wipro was the only major IT stock trading in the red, down 0.76 percent.

The rally followed a sharp decline in crude oil prices after reports that the United States and Iran paused military action over the weekend, reducing concerns over an extended energy shock and its inflationary impact. That improvement in the geopolitical outlook prompted investors to lower expectations of an imminent Fed rate increase.

According to CME FedWatch data cited in Reuters, markets priced in a 33.7 percent probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's policy meeting, down from 37.4 percent on Friday. Lower interest-rate expectations tend to support technology stocks because their valuations benefit from reduced discount rates.

Global markets reflected the improved sentiment: S&P 500 futures rose 0.7 percent and Nasdaq futures gained 1.1 percent, with technology shares leading gains ahead of a busy week of central bank meetings and corporate earnings.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said the temporary easing in geopolitical tensions had lifted investor sentiment and triggered a sharp retreat in crude oil prices. He noted that softer energy prices could help unwind inflationary pressures and support global growth expectations, reducing the likelihood of a more hawkish Fed stance while cautioning that Middle East developments would continue to influence markets.

Rajesh Palviya, Head of Research at Axis Direct, said Brent crude's sharp correction offered a significant tailwind for India through lower inflation expectations, an improved current account outlook and reduced pressure on the rupee. He added that the rebound in US index futures, particularly the Nasdaq, had strengthened investors’ risk appetite.

The combination of easing geopolitical risk, lower oil prices and reduced Fed hawkishness provided a favorable backdrop for Indian technology stocks, which have outperformed in risk-on market environments. Investors and analysts will closely watch upcoming central bank meetings and corporate earnings for further direction.
